tower's first release. Every tracker asks a person to say what is happening, and then drifts from the repository the moment attention lapses. fufu already knows: capture runs before every action, so the state trackers ask for is observable before anyone reports it. tower stores what a person authored — title, body, comments, links, a procedure stamp — and derives the rest. A flight is active because a branch exists with snapshots on it, not because anyone clicked. The consequence worth the whole design: tower sees work start before the first commit exists, because fufu's capture floor does. An agent that edits for twenty minutes and commits nothing is visible.

**A log of intent, a board derived**

Every verb appends one event to a log kept as ordinary git refs under `refs/tower/log/<author>/<writer>`, and every render folds that log fresh. Nothing is entered twice, no daemon runs, and a render never blocks on the network. `ff tower file` puts a flight on the board; `comment` and `link` land on its record; `edit` rewords a flight or a comment as a per-field overlay the fold applies in a third pass, so the log keeps every prior word. Bare `ff tower` is the board — an inbox in four sections matching four states of mind: waiting on you, in the air, holding, and open. A flight has two names, human against wire: the board prints `#3`, the wire carries `<writer>.<seq>`, and every verb takes either — a bare number resolves against the board, an ambiguous one refuses with the full forms, and a leading `#` is stripped so what tower prints pastes back in.

**The queue is passive**

tower is a thing agents call; it never calls agents. `ff tower next` claims the next ready flight — or with `-n <k>` a set of k that collide with neither each other nor anything already flying, judged by `ff collide` on real trees rather than declared file lists, and a pairing fufu could not judge excludes: unknown never rounds down to clear. The picked set is claimed in one atomic append, so two agents pulling at once cannot take the same flight, and `--peek` is the same computation with no claim written. An empty pick is an outcome riding a full data envelope, and only the exit code says which: 3 when the crew gate emptied it, 1 when the board is truly drained.

Around it, the lifecycle verbs: `claim` takes one specific flight out of order; `hold` stops one with a question attached and exits 3, bay intact, because a warm bay is the point of holding rather than abandoning; `answer` releases the hold; `done` finishes — off the board, on the record, comments still landing. `decompose` splits a flight into parts that file as flights of their own, riding ordinary link edges in one append, with the parent claimable — not finished — when the last part closes. If work should loop, the harness loops and calls `next` again: the harness is the scheduler, tower is only the queue.

**Bays**

`ff tower bay` is the pool: what is bootstrapped, what is occupied, what is free. `warm` takes a path, or bare mints the next slot under `tower.bays` — `bay-<n>`, smallest free number, foreign directories skipped rather than collided with. `release` captures a dirty tree before teardown and refuses an occupied bay whose flight is still open, naming the flight and the exit. `doctor` reads the drift — orphan chains, leftover branches — and observes and complains, never enforces.

**Procedures**

`procedures` lists what is installed by name and layer — built-in, or a repo's own fork under `.tower/procedures/`, which overrides the built-in whole and says so. A definition is copied into the log at filing, so editing an installed procedure never disturbs a flight already in the air. `triage` renders the unclassified pile bare, and with `-p` routes one flight: a single-part procedure stamps the flight itself, a multi-part one makes it a parent and files its parts in the same atomic batch; routing back to open is the undo, no special case.

**The seam**

tower is a separate program with its own store, authority, and cadence. It reads fufu over the CLI and the machine contract — `ff status --json`, `ff log --json`, `ff collide --json` — calls `ff worktree add|remove` tagged `--session <flight>`, and never links ff-core; nothing is written under `refs/fufu/*`, ever, which is fufu's extension rule unmodified. There is no bare tower binary: `ff tower` reaches `ff-tower` through fufu's `ff-<name>` dispatch, git-style, so the dependency stays honest — tower has nothing to say about a machine with no fufu on it.

`--json` on every verb swaps the human render for one line carrying the contract number, the verb, and either data or error, never both. Every refusal has an id that reads back through `ff tower explain`, with the raise site's exits beside it, so a coded failure never dead-ends. `config` is fufu's typed-registry model: only declared keys exist, arity decides, `--unset` returns to the default. `version` and `update` carry fufu's two-lane self-updater across — a passive notice on a cadence, an active verb that downloads, checksums, and swaps the binary — and an unofficial build refuses with the cargo line instead of guessing.

**Built and shipped like fufu**

Every verb has a hand-authored help page on fufu's model, and a clap-tree guard proves no command ships without one. CI runs the suite on Linux, macOS, and Windows; the suite went portable to get there — fakes run one POSIX sh dialect everywhere, under Git Bash through a `.cmd` trampoline on Windows; fixtures block the operator's git config entirely; paths are compared the way ff reports them. Release builds six native targets — linux, darwin, and windows on amd64 and arm64 — with `install.sh`, `install.ps1`, and a Homebrew tap formula riding the same artifact contract as fufu's.

**Numbers**

74 commits from an empty tree. Three crates, roughly 21,700 lines of Rust across 93 files. 395 workspace tests across 21 binaries, green on three operating systems. 20 verbs, 49 `ff tower explain` ids. Built against fufu at 0c4ab63f.
